title: Asset Protection: Lifecycle, Configuration and Change Management

header.html: 5.4 Understand asset protection: Asset lifecycle management (for example End Of Life (EOL) software and devices); Configuration and change management
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

html:
1Asset management

You cannot protect what you do not know you have. An asset inventory lists hardware, software, data, cloud services and AI models, each with an owner, location and classification.

Asset type Examples
Hardware Laptops, servers, network devices, IoT devices
Software Operating systems, applications, licenses
Data Databases, documents, AI training sets
Services Cloud accounts, AI services and bots
Exam tip

. Inventory first. Unknown or shadow assets are never patched or monitored.

2The asset life cycle

Stage Security actions
Acquire Check the vendor, requirements, secure by design
Deploy Harden, baseline configuration, record in the inventory
Operate and maintain Patch, monitor, back up, review access
Retire and dispose Remove from the network, sanitize data, recycle or destroy, update inventory

End of life (EOL) or end of support (EOS) means the vendor no longer provides security updates. EOL assets are high risk.

EOL response Fact
Replace or upgrade Best answer
Compensating controls Isolate, restrict access, monitor when replacement is not yet possible
Plan ahead Track support dates in the inventory
Exam tip

. EOL means no more patches. The best fix is to replace; isolation is only a stopgap.

3Configuration management

Configuration management keeps systems in a known, approved, secure state.

Concept Meaning
Baseline The approved secure configuration of a type of system
Hardening Removing unneeded services, accounts and software, changing defaults, closing ports
Configuration item Any component under control (a server, a setting)
Configuration management database (CMDB) Stores configuration items and their relationships
Drift Changes away from the baseline; detect and correct them

4Change management

Change management makes sure changes are requested, reviewed, approved, tested and recorded, so they do not break security or availability.

Step What happens
1 Request Describe the change and the reason
2 Assess Review impact and risk, including security
3 Approve A change advisory board (CAB) or manager approves
4 Test Try it in a test environment
5 Implement Carry it out in a planned window with a rollback plan
6 Review and document Verify success, update records and the baseline

Emergency changes are faster but still recorded and reviewed afterwards.

Patch management is change management for updates: find, test, deploy, verify. Critical vulnerabilities are patched first.

Exam tip

. No change without approval, testing and a rollback plan. Unauthorized changes break the baseline and are a risk.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1What should be done first to protect all of the assets of an organization?

  • ABuy a new firewall for the network
  • BWrite the final audit report
  • CEncrypt the oldest servers
  • DCreate and maintain an asset inventory
Show the answer

Answer: D. You cannot protect what you do not know you have, so an inventory comes first.

S2An old server runs software that the vendor no longer supports with security updates. What is the best long-term action?

  • AReplace or upgrade the unsupported software
  • BAdd more users to share the server load
  • CDisable logging to improve performance
  • DLeave the server unchanged and hope for the best
Show the answer

Answer: A. End-of-life software gets no patches, so replacement is the best answer; isolation is only temporary.

S3A retired laptop with customer data is given to charity. What must be done first?

  • ADelete the user profile and empty the recycle bin
  • BReset the password of the administrator account
  • CSanitize the storage so data cannot be recovered
  • DRemove the asset tag so it is not tracked
Show the answer

Answer: C. Data must be sanitized at disposal, and deleting files is not enough.

S4Which term describes the approved secure configuration used as the standard for a type of system?

  • AA drift
  • BA rollback
  • CA ticket
  • DA baseline
Show the answer

Answer: D. A baseline is the approved secure configuration; drift is a deviation from it.

S5A developer wants to change a firewall rule in production right away. What does change management require?

  • AMake the change now and tell the manager much later in the week
  • BAsk a colleague to make the change quietly
  • CWait until an incident happens before changing it
  • DRequest, assess, approve, test and record the change
Show the answer

Answer: D. Changes follow a controlled process: request, assessment, approval, testing, implementation and documentation.

S6Which plan element lets a team undo a failed change?

  • AA password policy
  • BA rollback plan
  • CA risk register
  • DA retention schedule
Show the answer

Answer: B. A rollback plan describes how to return to the previous state.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What does EOL mean for a product?

Show the answer

The vendor no longer provides security updates.

R2What is a baseline?

Show the answer

The approved secure configuration.

R3What is configuration drift?

Show the answer

Changes away from the baseline.

R4What does a CAB do?

Show the answer

Reviews and approves changes.

R5What is hardening?

Show the answer

Removing unneeded services and changing defaults.

R6What are the asset life cycle stages?

Show the answer

Acquire, deploy, operate and maintain, retire and dispose.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Inventory know what you have; owner, location, classification
Life cycle acquire, deploy, operate and maintain, retire and dispose (sanitize)
EOL no patches; replace; isolate as a stopgap
Configuration baseline, hardening, CMDB, detect drift
Change request, assess, approve (CAB), test, implement with rollback, review
